$meta.description: System-templated tutor messages — Final Addendum §11. Used by the daily re-engagement cron AND by teacher action handlers when sending system-driven nudges on a teacher's behalf. Each top-level key is a stable template id; the value is a per-language slot keyed by ISO-ish language code. Phase 5 expansion (BE-F + BE-H) added bn + ur slots across every template and added the previously-missing encouragement + progression triggers.
$meta.interpolation: Templates use {{firstname}} for the learner's first name; the runtime renderer substitutes verbatim with no other interpolations. New variables MUST be added to renderTeacherMessageTemplate and called out in the comment alongside this meta block.
$meta.authoring: Joey + ESOL practitioner co-author each English template. Translations for non-en slots are deferred to a future Phase 19 — placeholder strings are intentionally empty so the renderer's fallback rule (empty ⇒ untranslated ⇒ fall back to en) reads unambiguously.
$meta.fallback_rule: Renderers MUST fall back to `en` when the requested language slot is empty or missing. Never display a partial template.
$meta.alias_rule: The legacy template id `dormant_re_engagement` is preserved as an alias for `re_engagement` so the existing cron call site keeps working without an edit. New code should prefer `re_engagement`.

re_engagement.$description: Sent by the daily re-engagement cron to dormant learners (no session in 15+ days, no system re-engagement in 14+ days). Brief, warm, action-oriented — the goal is to nudge a login, not to teach.
re_engagement.en: Hi {{firstname}}, it's been a couple of weeks since your last session. Just checking in — could we book a short session this week to pick up where we left off?

dormant_re_engagement.$description: DEPRECATED alias for `re_engagement`. The legacy reEngagementCron.service.ts still references this id; the JSON shape mirrors `re_engagement` exactly so a future call-site rename is a one-line change. Keep in sync if `re_engagement` is edited.
dormant_re_engagement.en: Hi {{firstname}}, it's been a couple of weeks since your last session. Just checking in — could we book a short session this week to pick up where we left off?

encouragement.$description: Phase 5 (BE-H). Sent by a teacher on the priority dashboard when a learner is showing P2-tier struggle markers (e.g. inactive 7–13 days OR low recent scores AND non-zero engagement). Warm acknowledgement that learning takes effort, plus a tiny achievable next step. Avoid sounding remedial — the learner should feel seen, not pitied.
encouragement.en: Hi {{firstname}}, just a note to say I've seen how much effort you've been putting in. ESOL is hard work and yours is showing. If you can fit one short session this week, I think you'll surprise yourself.

progression.$description: Phase 5 (BE-H). Sent when a learner has hit the criteria the AI tutor uses to flag readiness to progress (e.g. consecutive successful sessions at their current Stage 3 objective). Acknowledges the milestone and previews next steps. Does NOT promise a level change — teachers don't confirm levels; the org admin does.
progression.en: Hi {{firstname}}, your last few sessions have been really strong. I'm flagging this with your organisation so they can review whether you're ready to move on to the next level. Either way — well done.
